units.text: Apple protects a Safari user's identity online in iOS 27 and macOS 27 by preventing advertising firms from easily knowing who is accessing a webpage, and blocking some web traffic. Here's how it works.

Maintaining user privacy has been a core tenet of Apple's design philosophy for a very long time. While web surfing is one of the more challenging things to keep users anonymized while doing, Apple has worked on ways to try and keep the user's identity out of data broker's hands.
In an October 19 post to WebKit's blog, Apple explains the effort it goes through to minimize how much data is collected and how users are tracked.
Post-cookie era problem

Cross-site cookies have been blocked for six years already, preventing advertisers from using one cookie across multiple websites to view a person's browsing habits. Preventing cookies from being used as a persistent user identifier was a major step forward.
Techniques such as App Tracking Transparency have also helped at the app level to great success.
However, tracking industry firms are still building profiles about users to personalize online advertisements. All despite losing the ability to follow the same cookie's usage all over the Internet.
A new system is used, referred to as "identity resolution." Rather than using cookies of website owners, the technique instead collects email addresses from sites via third-party firms.
This happens when you use an email to log into a website, or if you sign up for a newsletter. That address is stored, an opaque tracking ID assigned to it, and that ID is sent to the webpage.
Blocking tracking services means an advertising profile about a user cannot be easily compiled - Image Credit: WebKit

That tracking ID is then used as a token to identify the user whenever they log in to that site in the future. A user's advertising profile can have multiple tracking IDs associated with it, so a user can still be tracked across multiple websites, just like cross-site cookies.
As usual, the third-party firms can collect personal data about the user to fill out the profile, known as an identity graph,

To Apple, email addresses are almost always a form of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), just like a phone number. While it is easy for users to use them to sign into websites, they are a form of identification for data brokers that can last years.

The problem in Apple's view is that users are supplying information for one intended purpose. They aren't doing so for further unstated purposes like building online profiles and tracking their online movements.

To be clear, Apple says that first-party personalization is not tracking, as in the website you hand your information to is not the problem. Apple's technology doesn't aim to stop that from happening.

The real problem is a third party that can use connected information across multiple sites to build a cross-device, cross-site, and cross-party identity graph. Something the first-party site cannot do alone.
Blocking identity resolution

To try and stop this cross-site tracking from happening, Apple explains that Safari and WebKit in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, and visionOS 27 block some network access. Specifically, the connections to identity resolution infrastructure, the firms that create the cross-site identity graph.

Apple says this is targeting third-party infrastructure firms that handle identity resolution. They aren't the first-party websites being accessed nor receive emails to handle standard user authentication, but firms that include invisible elements on webpages just for tracking purposes.
The technique blocks the email addresses from being sent to the identity resolution infrastructure in the first place. If the emails can't get through, a profile cannot be made or checked.
This block is done at the "domain" level. This means that, regardless of how the query or request is structured, Apple's blocks cannot be worked around.

For iCloud+ subscribers, there's also Hide My Email that does the same thing, but in a more literal sense. The emails it uses are unique to each new website, which means they cannot be tracked at all due to not having a common comparable element.

So far, Apple's techniques are working well, and in some cases, too well. In early October, it was revealed that an ad agency was blocked in its entirety by Apple, being classified as a blockable data broker.
It has complained to Apple, but it won't see a resolution until iOS 27.2 ships.

units.text: Apple still makes it too hard for third-party developers to launch alternatives to Apple Pay, despite loosening its grip on access to the NFC chip embedded in iPhones. That’s the claim made by the UK’s antitrust watchdog, the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA).
The CMA says developers have reported that the compromise terms offered by Apple still don’t make it practical to develop competitors to Apple Pay …

When Apple first started embedding an NFC chip in iPhones to enable contactless payment, only the Apple Wallet app could take advantage of this. Third-party apps could use the NFC chip for other purposes, but not for card payments.
That saw the iPhone maker facing antitrust action in multiple countries around the world. In a number of them, it’s been forced to unlock access to the chip, most notably in the EU.

In EU countries, developers can request an entitlement to get access by proving to Apple that they meet the industry standards and hold the licenses needed to process consumer payments. No fees are payable. Users are then allowed to choose the default wallet app that appears when they double-click the side button or hold their phone near a payment terminal.
In the UK, however, the CMA told Reuters that Apple hasn’t offered developers the same terms.

CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell said […] “We have ​heard that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions relating to Apple’s contactless technology make it too difficult for challengers to innovate and compete.”
View all comments

Accordingly, the regulator has opened a public consultation on its proposed loosening of Apple’s grip on the contactless payment chip. Apple has responded by rejecting the proposal, but saying that it will continue to work with the CMA.

“We do ⁠not ​believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an ​approach with lower privacy and security protections. We will continue to engage constructively to reach an outcome ​that is in the best interest of our users.”
9to5Mac’s Take

I see this very much like third-party app stores. While I understand Apple’s position, the company is ultimately likely to lose these battles and is showing no sign of skating to where the regulatory puck is headed.

It seems a needless battle given that the commercial risk to Apple is very limited – the vast majority of iPhone owners are exceedingly unlikely to change the defaults for either app store or wallet app when given the choice.

units.text: tvOS 27.2 is coming next week, bringing several new features to Apple TV 4K users—including some screen saver upgrades. Here’s what’s new.
#1: Shuffle option for screen savers
tvOS offers a variety of great screen savers across multiple categories, including Aerials, Memories & Slideshows, Portraits, and Snoopy.
But historically, you’ve had to choose just one of these categories for your Apple TV screen savers, thus missing out on all the others.
In tvOS 27.2, Apple has a new ‘Shuffle’ option which will cycle through all available screen savers—regardless of category—throughout the day.
I’ve always favored Apple’s beautiful selection of Aerials. But I love that now I can continue enjoying Aerials while also benefiting from the other screen saver categories too.
#2: Apple TV app supports sign language
For select movies and shows that support it, the Apple TV app now lets viewers toggle sign language options inside the player controls. Per Sigmund Judge:
Update: tvOS 27.2 Beta 3 confirms upcoming Sign Language options for both American (ASL) and British (BSL) – allowing access to sign language options in player controls on selected movies and shows.
— Sigmund Judge (@sigjudge) October 5, 2026
ASL (American Sign Language) and BSL (British Sign Language) are available, expanding accessibility for content in the Apple TV app.
#3: Custom screen savers from Photos library
If you want to curate Photos screen savers, tvOS 27.2 lets you do that in a new and convenient way.
When setting up screen savers in the Memories & Slideshows or Portraits categories, you’re now able to manually select the content that’s included from your iPhone or iPad.
View all comments
Thanks to this addition, you can enjoy Apple TV screen savers from Photos without being forced to let them access your full library.
Coming soon: Siri AI and HomePod surround sound
When the new Apple TV 4K (4th gen) arrives on November 13, it will include support for Siri AI and also a new four-speaker HomePod surround sound setup.
Siri AI is coming to Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd generation too, but it’s not yet available in tvOS 27.2.
tvOS 27.2 is now available in RC (release candidate) and is expected to ship next week to all users.

units.text: Apple says that American companies are supplying “critical materials and components” for both the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo. In all, it says that nearly 100 components across the two phones are produced by American companies in more than a dozen states.
The company has named two of its US supply chain partners, stating that one of them will be making tech used in the variable aperture camera in the iPhone 18 Pro …
Apple today announced one new partnership and a second expanded one through the American Manufacturing Program (AMP).

Through its American Manufacturing Program (AMP), Apple is partnering with Perryman Company, a Pennsylvania-based titanium producer, to supply titanium for Apple products, including iPhone Duo. Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics, headquartered in Delaware, to produce technology for the new variable aperture in the iPhone 18 Pro camera system — the most advanced Apple has ever made […]

“We’re thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer. “American ingenuity is vital to all our products, from the titanium crafted for iPhone Duo to breakthrough camera innovations in iPhone 18 Pro. We’re proud to work with Perryman and Qnity Electronics to continue expanding our American Manufacturing Program and support U.S. jobs.”

The company says it’s committing up to $100 million over the next three years to assist Perryman in making the grade 5 titanium used in the enclosure for the iPhone Duo. It says Qnity Electronics will be making a component used in the variable aperture lens of the iPhone 18 Pro.
Qnity, which joined the American Manufacturing Program in March, will produce advanced films essential to the new variable aperture camera system on iPhone 18 Pro.
Apple highlighted the work performed by five additional US suppliers:

Broadcom is expanding and modernizing its Fort Collins, Colorado, facility under a $1.5 billion capital investment announced in July, producing advanced radio frequency components for a wide range of Apple products. The multiyear agreement will produce more than 15 billion U.S.-made chips.

Corning, an Apple partner since the original iPhone in 2007, produces specialty glass for Apple in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, including Ceramic Shield. By the end of 2026, all of the cover glass for iPhone — including iPhone Duo — and Apple Watch sold worldwide will be produced at this facility.

Coherent continues building on its multiyear agreement with Apple, supplying new vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser technology from its Sherman, Texas, facility. This technology enables Face ID and other key features across iPhone and iPad, including the redesigned, even more useful Dynamic Island on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

TSMC’s Arizona fab continues to scale its production of advanced chips used across a range of Apple products, including iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch — producing more than 100 million chips for Apple in 2026. Construction on the north campus is progressing as Apple’s partnership with TSMC in Arizona grows.

Amkor Technology broke ground on its first high-volume packaging and test facility in Peoria, Arizona, in September 2025, and began shell construction earlier this year. Phases 1 and 2 of the project are expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 local hires. Apple will be one of the facility’s first customers, marking another step toward expanding the scope of U.S. advanced manufacturing.

The iPhone maker says the new partnerships include increased use of recycled materials, and that all of its direct suppliers are required to power their entire Apple manufacturing operations with renewable energy by the end of the decade.

units.text: Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo

With just three days to go until the iPhone Duo is released, Apple is getting ready for the launch. Behind the scenes, the App Store now has screenshots of Apple's built-in apps running on the Duo. We've seen some apps in marketing materials, but images of the ones we haven't seen give us an idea of what it will be like using the ‌iPhone Duo‌ day to day.
Many apps are shown in landscape orientation with an iPad-like interface that uses some of the screen real estate for sidebar navigation. Other apps use the full screen for more viewing space.
Some apps have a dual view that goes beyond sidebar navigation. In Contacts, the app is divided into a list of names and a view for editing information.

The Siri app doesn't have a traditional sidebar, but it also doesn't get a full split. The left part of the interface is a tiled view of conversations, while the full conversation can be viewed on the right.

The ‌iPhone Duo‌ adopts a vertical dock and vertical navigation bars on the right side of the display in both open and closed views. The exception is an open view with the ‌iPhone Duo‌ held vertically, similar to an iPad in portrait orientation. When positioned that way, navigation bars remain at the bottom of the interface.
Apple's screenshots don't show many apps in the unfolded vertical orientation, but it is a viewing option. Apple says it's ideal for apps that use the keyboard or for browsing in Safari.

Apps like Preview have palettes at the bottom for selecting tools, and those are combined with sidebars, navigation bars, or both. Markup editing gives a good preview of what drawing and photo editing apps will be like, with a large amount of display space paired with a bottom tool palette.
Apps that don't need large navigation bars have widescreen views that take up the whole display. Apps that do have navigation bars have an option to tap to hide the bar.
Floating popovers show up when you press and hold on an icon. The popovers aren't scaled up and take up less room on the display than they do on Apple's smaller iPhones.

When you're on the Home Screen, you'll see the Today view on the left of the display with your widgets, while app icons are on the right. The status bar is in the upper-right corner, and the Lock Screen icons like Flashlight and Camera are in the bottom right. The inner display doesn't have an always-visible Dynamic Island because there is no Face ID and the FaceTime camera is under the screen. Apple is still using the ‌Dynamic Island‌, which expands out from the side of the display for Live Activities and alerts. The outer display has a small vertical ‌Dynamic Island‌ that includes the camera cutout.
Most of the ‌App Store‌ screenshots have the ‌iPhone Duo‌ unfolded in landscape orientation, though some also show what apps will look like on the smaller outer display.

Apps will be able to transition quickly from open to closed and to different positions, and Apple made an effort to keep navigation buttons in the same place for a unified experience no matter how you're using it.

Open and closed aren't the only options for the ‌iPhone Duo‌. Few screenshots show the positions, but the Duo can be used laptop-style at an angle for watching videos or standing in a tent shape with the outer display visible. You can also use it partially open and held like a book.

Screenshots also don't show two apps used side by side or multiple windows of the same app like Safari, both of which are options. We'll see a deluge of ‌iPhone Duo‌ updates for third-party apps when the device comes out.
The ‌iPhone Duo‌ is launching on October 23, which is this Friday. We should be getting media reviews and first impressions as soon as tomorrow since we'll be two days out from release.
(Thanks, Alireza!)

units.text: Sony sold over 400 XR patents to Meta, which is bad news for the future of VR gaming on PlayStation. It will become a problem for Apple Vision Pro gamers.

The sale of patents between companies isn't a new phenomenon, but sometimes they have unintended side effects. In the case of patent transfers from Sony to Meta, it's a move that will impact Apple down the road.

In early October, as first reported by ZD Net Korea and translated by Road to VR, Sony sold a collection of 419 XR-related patents to Meta. After signing a Confirmatory Assignment agreement in December 2025, batches of patents were transferred from Sony to Meta.

The portfolio consisted of 180 U.S. patents and 239 patent-family filings, the latter being filed in other regions. Those patents covered a variety of topics, including processing for XR applications, head-mounted display designs, and other related hardware.
Neither Sony nor Meta has officially announced anything about the deal or transfers, nor has Sony discussed future VR hardware ambitions.
That said, supplies of the PlayStation VR 2 have been tight for months. Production of the headset and controllers has reportedly ended.
A small problem for Apple VR gaming
Patent transfers are sometimes a worry for companies that have to regularly deal with infringement lawsuits. For once, the problem here isn't as severe as that where Apple is concerned.
More, it's one about game controls on the Apple Vision Pro, and the company's future plans in that area.

In June 2025, reports revealed that PlayStation VR2 controller support was coming to the Apple Vision Pro as part of visionOS 26. By November 2025, you can also buy the controllers from Apple directly for $249.95.
PS VR2 controllers used with an Apple Vision Pro - Image Credit: Apple
Adding support for the PS VR2 controllers solved a small problem for Apple. It made the Apple Vision Pro more capable of gaming.

Apple designed the Apple Vision Pro to be primarily controlled by your voice and hand gestures. However, the vast majority of games in the VR space rely on some form of handheld controller, not a hand-tracking system.

By adding that support, Apple inherited an existing game controller system that works well, designed by a company with a long history in gaming. If Apple was going to support controllers from any company, it would be the one with massive gaming credentials.
The PS VR2 controllers were also stylish and mainly white, which also fit Apple's preferred color scheme.
The controllers are not a completely dead product yet, but the warning signs are there. Retail stock is dwindling.
Future fallout
The patent trade doesn't mean anything in a legal sense for the Apple Vision Pro just now. Supply will be an issue soon.
It means Apple has to think twice about any future decisions regarding VR controllers. Especially when Sony eventually decides to stop supplying them because its exhausted its stockpile.

The obvious way forward is for Apple to make it easier for third-party game controller manufacturers to support the Apple Vision Pro. It already supports practically any standard game controller on the market, so doing the same for VR isn't a massive stretch of the imagination
If there's another pair of suitable controllers being sold in the future by a major gaming company, Apple will seek to work with it instead.

A third way is for Apple to go it alone with its own VR game controllers. Code references in September revealed that there are two game controllers in development within Apple, though the more traditional type and not VR.

evidence.title: 触屏Mac、防水iPad 苹果月底还有一波大的？

units.text: 苹果今年这新品发布的节奏，多少有点停不下来了。。。九月份才刚发完 iPhone 18 Pro 系列和首款折叠屏 iPhone Duo，十月中旬又整了一场 “ Welcome home ”，一口气更新了智能家居中枢 HomeView、新款 HomePod mini 和 Apple TV。
本来托尼以为今年苹果的新品差不多就这些。
结果这才过去一礼拜，苹果又官宣了一场新品活动，时间定在 10 月 28 号，主题叫 “ Pro and Tell ”，玩的是美国小学生 " show and tell " 的梗，中文文案给译成了 " 高端局，高手来 "。
不过跟传统发布会不同，这次苹果并不打算搞一场线上直播，而是邀请部分媒体和博主到洛杉矶，直接上手体验新品，剩下没被邀请的媒体，以及屏幕前的我们，就等苹果当天发新闻稿。
按照彭博社记者 Mark Gurman 最近的爆料，这次苹果准备更新的产品，主要包括全新设计的 MacBook Pro、搭载 M6 芯片的入门款 MacBook Pro 和 iMac，以及新一代 iPad mini。
其中最值得关注的，还得是那台传了不知道多少年的触屏 MacBook Pro，按照爆料，新款 MacBook Pro 会首次用上 OLED 面板，同时支持触控操作 —— 没错，Mac 终于要上触屏了！
对于用惯了 Windows 触屏本的小伙伴来说，这事听着可能没啥稀奇的，毕竟早几年前，Windows 阵营就已经有不少能直接拿手指戳的笔记本了，但放到苹果身上，意义就完全不一样了。
要知道，当年乔布斯就明确反对过给传统笔记本配备垂直触摸屏。包括苹果后来也一直坚持，Mac 就该用键盘和触控板操作，想要直接拿手指点屏幕，那是 iPad 干的活，即便后来苹果给 MacBook Pro 加过 Touch Bar，也没打算让用户直接触碰主屏幕。
结果这么多年过去，连 iPad 都已经用上桌面级芯片、能接键盘和鼠标干活了，Mac 这边反倒终于要补上触屏。
只能说，苹果也算想通了（ 这么看 iPad 哪天吃上 macOS 也不是没可能~当然，新 MacBook Pro 并不是简单地把现有屏幕换成 OLED，再往上面叠一层触控模组。
根据爆料，苹果还会针对触屏重新调整 macOS 的部分交互，比如平时你用鼠标操作时，菜单和按钮还是原来的样子；但当你直接用手指点击屏幕，部分控件就会变得更大，方便触摸。
除此之外，像双指缩放、手指滑动滚动页面这些大家在 iPad 上早就用习惯的操作，也有望出现在新款 Mac 上，这样一来，以后用 Mac 看照片、滑网页，就不一定非得在触控板上操作。
不过苹果显然也不打算一步到位，把 Mac 做成另一台 iPad，至少从现有爆料来看，触屏更多是给鼠标、键盘和触控板增加一种辅助操作方式，而不是直接把 macOS 改造成平板系统。
毕竟真要让一套用了几十年的桌面系统全面适配手指操作，恐怕也不是改几个按钮就能解决的，所以严格来说这台触控 MacBook Pro 并没有违背苹果 “ 祖训 ”，它只是在祖训边缘反复试探~
而除了触屏，这次 MacBook Pro 的外观也终于准备动刀了。从 2021 年那次大改款算起，MacBook Pro 的设计已经沿用了五年，新款据说会进一步减轻重量，机身也会变薄一些，同时把顶部那块用了好几代的刘海屏，换成挖孔设计，并引入灵动岛。
也就是说，以后 Mac 顶部的摄像头区域，可能不再只是一个占地方的缺口，还能像 iPhone 那样用来展示一些实时信息和应用状态。
至于 OLED 屏幕本身，优势也很直接，相比现有的 mini-LED 屏幕，OLED 可以做到像素级独立发光，在显示纯黑画面时不需要依赖背光分区，黑位、暗场细节和光晕控制都有先天优势。
这点对于经常拿 Mac 剪视频、修照片，或者喜欢在电脑上看电影的小伙伴来说，还是挺有吸引力的，但 OLED 的实际亮度、功耗和长期使用表现能做到什么水平，还得等真机出来再看。
看到这里，可能有差友已经准备把手里的 MacBook Pro 挂闲鱼了，不过托尼建议你先别急。
按照爆料，这批 OLED 触屏 MacBook Pro 用的还是今年三月份发布的 M5 Pro 和 M5 Max，而不是 M6 Pro、M6 Max，也就是说，新机主要卖点不在性能，而在屏幕、外观和触控体验。
与此同时，苹果还准备给现有的 14 英寸入门款 MacBook Pro，以及 24 英寸 iMac 换上最新的 M6 芯片，只不过它们预计还是常规升级，外观基本不变，顶多给 iMac 增加几种新配色。
好家伙，普通版本 Mac 用上更新的 M6，定位更高的 OLED 触屏版 Mac 反倒继续用 M5 Pro 和 M5 Max —— 从这个安排来看，苹果更像是在现有专业本之上，又单独划出了一档产品。
至于 OLED 触屏版 Mac 的价格，恐怕也不会太客气，今年三月份发布的 M5 Pro 版 14 英寸 MacBook Pro，国行起售价已经到了 17999 元，M5 Max 版本更是接近三万元起步。
如果这次 OLED 触屏版真像爆料说的那样，定位比现款还高，那价格继续往上涨，恐怕也是大概率事件，想尝鲜的小伙伴，钱包得提前做好准备了。。。
相比之下，这次另一台新品，反而更值得关注 —— 它就是两年没更新的 iPad mini。
别看现在大屏手机动不动就往七英寸靠，iPad mini 这种小尺寸平板，还是有一批相当忠实的用户，有人喜欢拿它躺床上看漫画、刷视频，有人把它当随身阅读器，也有人买来打游戏。
但现款 iPad mini 有个绕不开的问题，就是屏幕 —— 都已经卖到这个价位了，你敢信它居然还在用一块 60Hz 的 LCD 屏幕，尤其跟现在一众高刷安卓平板放在一起，确实有点不够看。
好消息是，这次苹果终于准备给 iPad mini 换上 OLED，而且按照目前的爆料，新一代 iPad mini 8 除了换屏，还会把芯片升级到 A20 Pro，并将前置摄像头从竖屏方向挪到横屏方向。
这样以后横着拿平板视频通话，摄像头位置也会更自然，不至于总像在从侧面拍人。
不过坏消息是，虽然有供应链信源确认了新 iPad mini 屏幕总成驱动是 120Hz，但是苹果可能会通过固件限制把它的刷新率锁回 60Hz，主打一个等级森严，就看它愿不愿意大方一把了。
当然，这次 iPad mini 还有一项挺有意思的变化，就是防水。据爆料，苹果给新款 iPad mini 设计了一套新的扬声器结构，通过振动机身表面来发声，减少开孔，以此改善整机的防水能力，如果消息属实，它可能成为苹果第一款支持防水的 iPad。
至于价格，按照 Gurman 的说法，新款 iPad mini 因为 OLED 和结构升级，售价可能会明显提高，他甚至估计美版起售价会从目前的 599 美元涨到接近 799 美元，涨幅确实不小。。。
这样的话，感觉 iPad mini 还是应该还是支持高刷的，不然说不过去。
说到这里，这次苹果准备端上来的新品，基本就盘得差不多了，根据目前的消息，新设备将在 10 月 28 日正式公布，并在 11 月 6 日左右正式开卖，不过具体开售节奏仍要等官方确认。
反正距离 10 月 28 日也没几天了，接下来就看苹果还能给我们留多少惊喜。

units.text: Apple has announced new and extended partnerships with US firms to manufacture titanium for its iPhone enclosures and variable aperture technology for the iPhone 18 Pro.

Apple's American Manufacturing Program (AMP) has already seen the company investing in firms across the country. One of those has been Qnity Electronics, and now Apple has announced that it is extending its partnership with this Delaware-based firm.
It's also revealed a new partnership with Pennsylvania's Perryman Company, a producer of titanium. Its titanium is to be used in the iPhone Duo and unspecified other devices.

"We're thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America," said Sabih Khan, Apple's chief operating officer, in a statement. "American ingenuity is vital to all our products, from the titanium crafted for iPhone Duo to breakthrough camera innovations in iPhone 18 Pro."
"We're proud to work with Perryman and Qnity Electronics to continue expanding our American Manufacturing Program and support US jobs," he continued.

Apple says it will commit up to $100 million to the deal with Perryman over the next three years. The company melts, forges, and rolls titanium with a minimum of 80% recycled content for the iPhone Duo.
The expanded work with Qnity Electronics is said to specifically concern the new variable aperture camera now being used in the iPhone 18 Pro.
Apple says that it now works with suppliers across all 50 states and that this supports over 450,000 American jobs.

This new announcement is a continuation of the initially $500 billion manufacturing investment announced in 2025. Apple has subsequently raised this figure to $600 billion, with the project set to run over four years.

用户将万事达卡绑定 Apple Pay 后，无需携带实体卡，即可在境外通过 iPhone 、Apple Watch 等苹果设备完成支付。
IT之家注意到，万事达卡还为绑定 Apple Pay 的客户带来了一系列优惠：首绑并消费享至高 5 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 33.5 元人民币）返现、境外消费满 10 笔抽 500 元礼遇、境外交通至高免单优惠、环球赏精选商户至高返 50%。

Even as Apple challenges the $5.7 billion verdict set by a jury in the Taction patent case, the company hopes to squeeze out more. A jury ruled that Apple violated two patents, though not willingly, and Apple denied any wrongdoing.

According to a report from Reuters, Taction has asked a federal judge for hundreds of millions more in payment from Apple. It argues that the damages only cover from 2021 to March 2026 and should cover the previous six months as well.
Taction has also asked for prejudgment interest at California's 7% statutory rate. The interest on $5.7 billion would be an incredible figure on top of the already large sum.
The argument is simple. Taction says "the size of the jury's award is no reason to withhold interest."
Of course, Apple plans to appeal and has already challenged the jury's verdict. It was allegedly made without any materials to accurately determine the damages payment.
Plus, the logic of the case and the alleged infringement are contradictory. Apple hopes it can have the whole thing thrown out with a summary judgment, but no verdict has been shared yet.

Apple showcases 2026 Designers of Tomorrow
Apple today published an interesting press release highlighting the work of five designers, who “integrated Apple products into their creative processes” to develop their projects.

Now in its second year, Apple’s “Designers of Tomorrow” initiative is organized in partnership with Design Miami. As Apple explains, this year’s participants were selected by a jury that included the company’s vice president of industrial design, Molly Anderson.
Here’s Apple on this year’s theme and the designers’ approach to it:

“Apple’s Designers of Tomorrow showcase, in collaboration with Design Miami, returns for a second year to spotlight the best in emerging talent, this time focusing on the theme of presence. Exploring what still holds the public’s attention amid the hurried pace of the modern world, designers Salem S. Charabi, Isabel Rower, Yoonjeong Lee, and Parafernalia (Genki Matsumura and Sebastián Zorrilla) crafted original works that invite reflection and aim to shift perspectives, engage the senses, and kindle curiosity.”

According to Rodman Primack, the program’s curator, the artists’ works “demonstrate the power of objects to shape our physical environments and transform the human experiences that are possible within them.”

苹果当天宣布与两家美国企业建立或扩大合作关系。其中，位于宾夕法尼亚州的钛金属制造商Perryman Company将为苹果供应钛材料。苹果计划在未来三年内向该公司投入最高1亿美元，用于生产包括iPhone Duo在内的多款产品所需钛金属材料。
苹果表示，iPhone Duo采用第5级钛金属机身结构，以提升设备强度和耐用性。Perryman将在宾夕法尼亚州工厂负责相关钛材料的生产制造。
与此同时，总部位于特拉华州的Qnity Electronics将参与iPhone 18 Pro全新可变光圈相机系统的关键部件生产。该公司将制造用于该相机系统的先进薄膜材料，而苹果将这一可变光圈系统称为其迄今最先进的手机影像技术之一。
苹果首席运营官萨比赫·汗表示，从iPhone Duo所使用的钛金属到iPhone 18 Pro搭载的创新相机技术，美国企业正在为苹果最新产品提供越来越多的重要材料与核心组件。公司将继续扩大美国制造计划，并支持更多本土就业机会。
苹果称，目前美国企业已为iPhone Duo和iPhone 18 Pro生产近100种组件和材料，相关供应链覆盖十多个州。公司表示，其供应商网络已经遍布美国全部50个州，并支撑超过45万个工作岗位。
除Perryman与Qnity外，苹果还介绍了多家美国供应商的最新进展。博通正在扩建位于科罗拉多州的工厂，根据今年7月公布的15亿美元投资计划，该设施未来将生产超过150亿颗美国制造芯片，并为苹果提供先进射频组件。
长期合作伙伴康宁则继续在肯塔基州生产用于苹果设备的特种玻璃，包括Ceramic Shield超瓷晶面板。苹果预计，到2026年底，全球销售的全部iPhone（包括iPhone Duo）以及Apple Watch所使用的外层保护玻璃都将由该工厂生产。
激光技术供应商Coherent也正在扩大与苹果的合作，从得克萨斯州工厂提供新一代垂直腔面发射激光器技术。这些组件被用于Face ID等功能，并将应用于iPhone 18 Pro系列重新设计后的灵动岛组件。
在芯片领域，苹果再次强调与台积电亚利桑那州工厂的合作。按照计划，该工厂将在2026年为苹果生产超过1亿颗芯片，覆盖iPhone、iPad和Apple Watch等产品线。随着合作规模扩大，亚利桑那州北部厂区建设也在持续推进。
此外，封装与测试企业Amkor Technology正在亚利桑那州建设大型先进封装测试设施。苹果表示，自己将成为该工厂首批客户之一，项目建成后预计可支持超过3500个当地就业岗位。
苹果还强调，新合作项目不仅扩大美国本土制造规模，也将提高回收材料的使用比例。与此同时，公司要求所有直接供应商在本十年结束前实现苹果产品制造过程全面使用可再生能源供电，以配合其长期环保目标。
此次公布的供应链进展，也是苹果“美国制造计划”的最新成果。该计划旨在推动更多关键零部件和先进制造能力回流美国本土，并进一步强化苹果在材料、芯片、玻璃、传感器和先进封装等核心领域的供应链布局。

units.text: CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced new and expanded partnerships with American companies that are supplying critical materials and components for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro. Through its American Manufacturing Program (AMP), Apple is partnering with Perryman Company, a Pennsylvania-based titanium producer, to supply titanium for Apple products, including iPhone Duo. Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics, headquartered in Delaware, to produce technology for the new variable aperture in the iPhone 18 Pro camera system — the most advanced Apple has ever made. Apple works with suppliers in all 50 states and supports more than 450,000 American jobs. Last year, the company deepened that commitment by launching AMP, aimed at bringing even more advanced manufacturing and critical component production to the United States as part of Apple’s $600 billion, four-year commitment to U.S. manufacturing and innovation. “We’re thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer. “American ingenuity is vital to all our products, from the titanium crafted for iPhone Duo to breakthrough camera innovations in iPhone 18 Pro. We’re proud to work with Perryman and Qnity Electronics to continue expanding our American Manufacturing Program and support U.S. jobs.”

The grade 5 titanium enclosure on iPhone Duo is exceptionally strong, providing amazing durability to the first foldable iPhone. Apple will commit up to $100 million over the next three years with Perryman, a family-owned business and a global leader in manufacturing specialty titanium products. At its site in Houston, Pennsylvania, Perryman melts, forges, and rolls titanium with a minimum of 80 percent recycled content for iPhone Duo.
Apple is committing up to $100 million over the next three years with Perryman, which will supply titanium for products such as iPhone Duo.

Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics to build key camera technology for iPhone 18 Pro in the U.S. Qnity, which joined the American Manufacturing Program in March, will produce advanced films essential to the new variable aperture camera system on iPhone 18 Pro. Variable aperture is at the heart of the new 48MP Fusion Main camera, which enables incredible light and depth control. It’s powered by on-device intelligence that automatically lets in more light for darker settings and helps get sharper detail in brighter ones.
Apple is expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics to produce camera technology for the new variable aperture system on iPhone 18 Pro.

Nearly 100 components in iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro — from wireless chips to the silicon that powers key functions across the devices — are produced by American companies and drawn from suppliers in more than a dozen states. That footprint continues to grow, empowering partners across the country to bring new capabilities online:

Broadcom is expanding and modernizing its Fort Collins, Colorado, facility under a $1.5 billion capital investment announced in July, producing advanced radio frequency components for a wide range of Apple products. The multiyear agreement will produce more than 15 billion U.S.-made chips.

Corning, an Apple partner since the original iPhone in 2007, produces specialty glass for Apple in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, including Ceramic Shield. By the end of 2026, all of the cover glass for iPhone — including iPhone Duo — and Apple Watch sold worldwide will be produced at this facility.

Coherent continues building on its multiyear agreement with Apple, supplying new vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser technology from its Sherman, Texas, facility. This technology enables Face ID and other key features across iPhone and iPad, including the redesigned, even more useful Dynamic Island on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

TSMC’s Arizona fab continues to scale its production of advanced chips used across a range of Apple products, including iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch — producing more than 100 million chips for Apple in 2026. Construction on the north campus is progressing as Apple’s partnership with TSMC in Arizona grows.

Amkor Technology broke ground on its first high-volume packaging and test facility in Peoria, Arizona, in September 2025, and began shell construction earlier this year. Phases 1 and 2 of the project are expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 local hires. Apple will be one of the facility’s first customers, marking another step toward expanding the scope of U.S. advanced manufacturing.

As part of Apple’s ambitious goal to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030, all direct suppliers are required to power their Apple manufacturing with renewable energy by the end of this decade. These partnerships, which also include the increased use of recycled materials, reflect that broader environmental commitment. Apple’s commitment to American manufacturing extends to the workers and businesses building the sector’s future. In August, Apple opened its Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston, Texas — the company’s second U.S. manufacturing learning site. Inside the 20,000-square-foot center, Apple engineers train small- and medium-sized businesses on the same processes used to make Apple products, from advanced manufacturing principles for final assembly to design considerations for printed circuit board assembly. The AMC sits within the same Houston facility that builds Apple’s advanced AI servers and will begin manufacturing Mac mini this year.

units.text: Apple’s Designers of Tomorrow showcase, in collaboration with Design Miami, returns for a second year to spotlight the best in emerging talent, this time focusing on the theme of presence. Exploring what still holds the public’s attention amid the hurried pace of the modern world, designers Salem S. Charabi, Isabel Rower, Yoonjeong Lee, and Parafernalia (Genki Matsumura and Sebastián Zorrilla) crafted original works that invite reflection and aim to shift perspectives, engage the senses, and kindle curiosity. “The theme was born from an honest recognition of just how busy our lives have become,” says Rodman Primack, the program’s curator and former longtime creative director of Design Miami. “In answering it, our designers demonstrate the power of objects to shape our physical environments and transform the human experiences that are possible within them.” This year’s participants were handpicked by a jury of global design voices — including Alexandra Cunningham Cameron, Fabien Cappello, Jennifer Dunlop Fletcher, Minjae Kim, Hun Chung Lee, Marion Mailaender, Nifemi Marcus-Bello, Jennifer Roberts, and Apple’s Molly Anderson — for their storytelling, material innovation, and craft. Their work also highlights Apple’s dynamic role in the creative process, empowering designers at every level to capture, refine, and share their ideas with the world. “Apple products continue to emerge as a through line so many extraordinary designers share, spanning disciplines, cultures, and processes,” explains Primack. “It’s a testament to how seamlessly these products and tools can integrate into any workflow.” Ahead of the exhibition, which opens today at Hôtel de Maisons in Paris, the featured designers discussed their final pieces and the tools they used to bring them to life. Egyptian Danish architect Salem S. Charabi blends old-world practices and the latest digital tools to create timeless pieces, and his Designers of Tomorrow project, The Eminence of Light, is no exception. “Light is something we’re all instinctively drawn to, dating back to our earliest fires,” Charabi notes. “A lantern felt like the perfect encapsulation of this idea — a reflection of our capacity to light up the world.”
The project’s delicate skeleton of meticulously stacked date palm fronds provides a satisfying contrast to the limestone base.
The project’s delicate skeleton of meticulously stacked date palm fronds provides a satisfying contrast to the limestone base.

Charabi constructed the lantern’s veil from banana paper, applying Japanese methods to Egyptian palms. A delicate skeleton of meticulously stacked date palm fronds provides a satisfying contrast to the limestone base, which carries the traces of its own formation in its grooves. “Each strand is an octagon in profile — just 3 millimeters wide, split by hand, and carefully drilled,” Charabi explains. “The ends are then sharpened with a chisel to interlock.” Both the lamp and the audience’s attention are suspended by the same tension. The resulting piece feels at once deeply natural and finely engineered. “For this project, every component had to be mapped out in detail,” Charabi says. “I sketched and did all the 3D modeling on my MacBook Pro. It was a complex process getting everything to fit just right — from the carving of the stone and the paper molds, down to the delicate base.” By blending familiar forms with the unexpected, Brooklyn-based designer Isabel Rower cultivates presence and transforms everyday objects into active sensory experiences. “The surface functions as a site for curiosity for me,” explains Rower. “People don’t always know what my pieces are made of, even as they’re touching them. It’s captivating when something that isn’t readily understood takes the form of a familiar object, like a table or teapot. It generates a kind of friction that brings you into immediate awareness of the objects we use every day.”
Rower’s Padded Chair 1860 draws on 18th- and 19th-century papier-mâché furniture and objets d’art. Its high-gloss finish stands in sharp contrast to the beaded fringe lining the seat.
Rower’s Padded Chair 1860 draws on 18th- and 19th-century papier-mâché furniture and objets d’art. Its high-gloss finish stands in sharp contrast to the beaded fringe lining the seat.

This intrigue is captured by her piece Padded Chair 1860, whose dramatic proportions draw on 18th- and 19th-century papier-mâché furniture and objets d’art. Its high-gloss finish stands in sharp contrast to the beaded fringe lining the seat. “The ceramic beads make a sound when brushed, drawing attention to both the material and its form, turning the unconscious act of sitting down into a mindful encounter,” Rower says. Apple is a fixture throughout her creative process. “I use iPhone to capture quick thoughts and document my process, AirPods Pro to listen to music, and MacBook Pro to build my personal visual archive,” says Rower. “I’ll also use Keynote to juxtapose ideas and explore the relationship between images and text.” For Seoul-based designer Yoonjeong Lee, presence begins with quiet discovery. Through material transformation, she repositions overlooked background objects as central subjects. Her piece New Form showcases a trio of worn-down pencils that have been given new life as nails. “I wanted to express this year’s theme through something small that we could all recognize — a shared experience,” Lee explains. “This story doesn’t carry some grand narrative. Instead, it takes a second look at the familiar to help you rediscover that which has been quietly forgotten.”
Lee’s New Form doubles as a wooden table and lamp, and features worn-down pencils that serve as nails.
Lee’s New Form doubles as a wooden table and lamp, and features worn-down pencils that serve as nails.

The base of the piece doubles as a wooden table and lamp. Sheets of paper serve as a lampshade, softly diffusing the light below, while the pencils hold them firmly in place. Applying her signature technique of building volume through repetition, Lee stacked roughly 5,000 thin sheets of veneer to construct the wooden base. Lee’s focus on overlooked structural elements extends to her workflow, where she credits iCloud, AirDrop, and Notes for keeping her process seamless. “I often use iPad Pro and Apple Pencil to create a sketch and jot down quick thoughts, but it’s how my devices connect to each other that makes them, and all their flexible features, truly useful,” she explains. Founded by Genki Matsumura and Sebastián Zorrilla, Parafernalia is a design studio that spans from Monterrey to Mexico City. The duo’s creative process is driven by constant dialogue, questioning, and iteration, often powered by FaceTime. “For us, presence can take many forms,” says Matsumura. “We experience it with ourselves, with our surroundings, and with others. Our piece explores how all these expressions can coexist within a single object.”
The project mirrors the studio’s workflow: two designers relying on iPhone and iPad Pro to trade sketches and track progress in real time.
The project mirrors the studio’s workflow: two designers relying on iPhone and iPad Pro to trade sketches and track progress in real time.

Their piece MonoAmbiente 1 considers presence as both a personal relationship with one’s surroundings and a collective act. When closed, its acid-etched stainless steel surface forms a vast landscape. Its dual state invites the observer not only to examine it but to experience it. Once expanded, it reveals stools and a table, turning a distant scene into an intimate setting where two people can converse, play chess, or share a drink. The project mirrors the studio’s workflow: two designers relying on iPhone and iPad Pro to trade sketches and track progress in real time. “We don’t share a physical desk. Our studio is iCloud,” Matsumura explains. By using Messages, FaceTime, and Procreate, they bridge the geographic gap. “Apple plays an integral part in how we think, design, and communicate. In many ways, it’s how we cultivate presence with each other.”

当用户尝试在苹果官网或Apple Store应用中购买超过两部iPhone Duo时，系统会弹出提示，要求将订单中的iPhone Duo数量调整至两台及以下后才能继续结账。提示信息显示：“每位客户最多可购买2台iPhone Duo，请在结账前调整订单中的iPhone Duo总数量。”
目前尚不清楚这一限制是否在10月16日预售开启时便已存在。一些Reddit用户表示，该限制是后来新增的措施。不过，也有用户称自己此前成功下单了四台iPhone Duo，而另一些用户则表示从一开始就受到两台上限的限制，因此具体实施时间仍无法得到确认。
事实上，苹果此前已经在中国、新加坡和中国香港等市场明确规定每位消费者最多购买两台iPhone Duo。但在美国市场，苹果官网并未提前公开说明这一限制，只有当用户尝试将超过两台设备加入购物车时，系统才会显示相关提示。
iPhone Duo开启预售后市场需求极为旺盛。预售开始仅数分钟，首发日配送库存便迅速售罄，大量消费者获得了11月甚至12月的预计交付日期。随着苹果持续调整供应链和产能，部分用户近期已经发现自己的预计发货时间有所提前。

units.text: Apple today began selling repair parts for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, as well as the M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studio and the M6 or M5 Pro Mac mini models. Here are the details.
Parts and tools now available for new iPhones and Macs

Apple launched its Self Service Repair program in 2022, allowing users in eligible regions to purchase replacement parts and buy or rent the tools needed to perform their own repairs on supported devices.
Additionally, Apple offers official repair manuals for several products, with detailed, step-by-step instructions on the replacement procedures for each serviceable part or component.

Today, Apple expanded the Self Service Repair Store to include replacement parts and tools for several recently released devices. The update comes on the same day that Apple announced new and expanded partnerships with US suppliers producing components for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.
For iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max owners, this means they can now purchase replacement parts and tools for the following components:
Back glass
Battery
Bottom speaker
Camera
Display
Enclosure
Front camera
Logic board
Main microphone
Other parts
SIM tray
Taptic Engine
Top speaker

Selecting a category brings up the available replacement parts, along with tools and other supplies needed for the procedure, such as adhesive cutters, suction cups, nylon probes, adhesive removal tools, torque drivers, and screws. These items can also be purchased separately.

For those who are curious, the replacement camera costs $249, unchanged from last year’s models, despite the addition of a new variable-aperture system to the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Apple also offers a $59.76 credit for returning the original camera, bringing the effective cost down to $189.24.
For the Mac Studio (M5 Max and M5 Ultra), Apple now offers replacement parts for everything from Thunderbolt and USB-C ports to fans, speakers, SSD modules, logic boards, and power supplies.
The Mac mini (M6 and M5 Pro) has a somewhat shorter list, covering components such as fans, speakers, logic boards, batteries, and power supplies, among others.
You can learn more about Apple’s Self Service Repair Store here, and you can find the company’s official repair manuals here.

▲ 图源：华为官网 | HUAWEI Pura X View
IT之家附新版本更新日志如下：
华为分享
隔空传送新玩法，握拳抓取内容后，旋转拳头背对屏幕可触发“仅一次查看”功能，分享内容接收方仅可查看一次。
通信共享
通信共享功能再升级，手机与搭载 HarmonyOS 7 的手机、平板、鸿蒙电脑之间支持多人互助通信共享，通过碰一碰或者登录同一华为账号共享网络建立互助网络，在移动网络信号弱或网络负载大等场景下可获得更快、更稳的网络体验。
畅连
畅连实时对讲支持查找好友功能，在实时对讲位置共享的过程中，当好友在附近时，点击好友头像上的查找标识，便可根据指引快速找到好友，户外碰头、商场找人不迷路。
系统
1.支持通过 iPhone 的“鸿蒙星河互联”应用与 iPhone 互联，实现消息相互流转 / 设备相互查找 / 网络共享。
2.新增实况窗分享功能，实况窗卡片左滑后点击分享按钮，可通过华为分享、畅连等场景分享至联系人（部分应用实况窗支持）。
3.支持应用将关键信息以悬浮窗口、悬浮胶囊、固定滚动条、横幅卡片形态常驻屏幕，以便实时关注与便捷操作，如实时跟踪股票动态，实现全场景轻量化盯盘（部分应用支持）。
4.优化部分场景系统稳定性。
相机
优化相机拍摄后点击缩略图预览的使用体验。
图库
优化图库稳定性及部分界面的显示效果。
蓝牙
优化部分蓝牙场景的使用体验。
需要注意的是，华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 系统常采取分批方式进行推送，未收到推送需继续等待。部分用户有快速升级的需求，可以通过“设置-软件更新-检查更新”尝试下载版本进行升级。

units.text: New Apple TV 4K Features 'Whole Room Audio' With Four HomePods

The new fourth-generation Apple TV 4K announced last week can connect to up to four HomePods in front-left, front-right, rear-left, and rear-right positions, enabling an all-Apple surround sound system for home theater setups. There is also a related new feature that has not received as much attention: Whole Room Audio.
Apple says the Whole Room Audio feature spreads sound evenly across four HomePods in a room.

"Whole Room Audio spreads sound evenly across four HomePod speakers for audio that's perfect for parties or game day," says Apple. "Everything from music to sports commentary comes through clearly, no matter where you are in the room."

According to the user "pdfu," who has been digging into Apple's software code in recent months, "Surround Sound" and "Whole Room Audio" will be separate options in tvOS 27.2's audio settings when four HomePods are connected to the new Apple TV 4K.

You'll get new audio controls when you set up four HomePods with the new Apple TV. Speaker Mode: Surround Sound or Whole Room Audio. Specifically for Surround Sound: • Spatialize Stereo: Control whether to play a spatially processed mix for video and music. As reported in September, when disabled, normal stereo plays on the front speakers, while rear speakers receive an empty mix. Defaults to On for Video and Music. • Surround Level: Adjust the rear pair relative to the fronts. Supports −8 dB through +8 dB, in 0.5 dB steps. Defaults to Normal (0 db). There are no audio options for Whole Room Audio, as it uses stereo channels for both speaker pairs. The channels are assigned diagonally: front-left and rear-right share the left channel, while front-right and rear-left share the right channel. — pdfu (@itspdfu) October 19, 2026

When enabled, "pdfu" said Whole Room Audio assigns the same left or right stereo channel to HomePods positioned diagonally opposite each other. This arrangement is designed to provide a more consistent stereo listening experience throughout a room, regardless of where you are standing or which direction you are facing. As mentioned by Apple, the feature is ideal for parties, where people might not always be facing the TV.
"Whole Room Audio" was previously referred to as "Party Mode" in rumors.

You can connect four of the new HomePod mini 2 speakers to the new Apple TV 4K, or you can mix and match pairs of HomePod mini 2 and full-sized HomePod 2 speakers, so long as the front and rear pairs of speakers match. For example, you can have two full-sized HomePod 2 speakers up front and two HomePod mini 2 speakers in the rear.
Previous-generation Apple TV 4K models remain limited to two HomePods for stereo sound.
The new Apple TV 4K launches on Friday, November 13, while the HomePod mini 2 launches on Friday, October 30. Both devices can be pre-ordered now.

units.text: Apple is looking for an experienced cellular modem systems engineer to help develop its next generation of cellular modems as the company transitions toward 6G. Here are the details.
‘A rare opportunity to shape the future of wireless communication’

As spotted by MacRumors, Apple listed a new job opening yesterday for a 6G Cellular Modem Systems Engineer, with a base salary range of $175,000 to $308,500 per year, plus stock awards and other benefits.
From the job listing:

We’re looking for a Cellular Modem Systems Engineer to join our cellular systems engineering team as we define and build the next generation of cellular technology. This is a rare opportunity to shape the future of wireless communication at a company that ships at global scale as we transition towards 6G. In this role, you’ll bring an end-to-end view of wireless systems — spanning 3GPP standards, feature definition and planning, design, hardware and software architecture and partitioning — to deliver leading-edge performance and power optimizations and features that directly improve the user experience across Apple products. If you thrive at the intersection of deep technical theory and hands-on bring-up — and you’re excited about pushing beyond 5G into the 6G era — we want to hear from you.

Apple says the candidate’s responsibilities will include defining features and requirements for next-generation cellular modems, designing algorithms to improve performance and power efficiency, and working with hardware and software teams to bring those technologies to market.
The candidate should have a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field, along with at least 10 years of industry experience working with cellular technologies.
Apple also requires a strong understanding of cellular communication standards and proficiency in MATLAB, C/C++, or Python.

Interestingly, Apple also lists experience with generative AI and LLM-based tools “to accelerate engineering workflows” as a minimum qualification. Ideally, the candidate should also have a track record of published research or patents in wireless communications, among other preferred qualifications.
For context, 6G is still years away and in the early stages of development, as companies and industry organizations work to define what it will look like.

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) has outlined potential peak speeds of up to 200 Gbps, compared to 5G’s theoretical maximum of 20 Gbps, along with research targets for latency as low as 0.1 milliseconds.
AI is also expected to play a much bigger role in 6G, helping networks automatically adjust to changing conditions, optimize signal quality, manage traffic, and reduce power consumption.
The first official 6G technical specifications are expected to be finalized in late 2028, with commercial networks and compatible devices anticipated around 2030.
You can find more details about the position in Apple’s full job listing here.

units.text: Last week TIME shared select quotes from a new interview with Apple CEO John Ternus, but today the full video has been published, including a discussion on Ternus’s involvement with Apple’s design teams.
John Ternus says that at Apple ‘design means everything to us’
Ever since John Ternus officially became CEO last month, reporting has indicated that he’s spending lots of his time hands-on with Apple’s design teams.
In a recent interview with TIME, Ternus discusses his new role, the transition, and his current priorities. And design comes up in the conversation.
At one point he’s asked directly: “How involved with design are you still?”
Here’s what Ternus said:

It’s funny because as a product designer—I’m a mechanical engineer by background—the team that the product designers work most closely with are the industrial designers. So, I’ve been working hand in hand with industrial designers at Apple since I started. And it’s an amazing relationship.

I think what’s so special about this place is design is at the center of it. Design means everything to us. And what’s incredible is our designers, both on the software side and the hardware side, they really understand the engineering. And the engineers have a very deep appreciation for design. And so it’s a really powerful collaboration. It’s not [like] a designer sketches something up and then throws it over the wall and says, “Go make that.” From the very beginning the teams are collaborating, and it’s just a wonderful thing to be a part of.

Without explicitly saying that he’s been especially hands-on with the design teams, Ternus emphasizes that he’s always worked closely with Apple designers, and reiterates how central design is to the company.

units.text: 微博用户Kang近日发布视频称，iPhone Duo内屏铰链上方的区域触感偏软，手指按压时会略微下陷，表面还可能出现短暂皱纹；移开手指后，屏幕似乎会恢复平整。数台设备据称都出现相同现象，但目前这只是用户实测和社交媒体转述，尚无独立耐久性测试，也不能据此判断设备存在缺陷。
苹果已公布的iPhone Duo内屏结构显示，面板上下均有高强度玻璃，表面覆盖耐刮涂层和纳米纹理聚合物保护层，苹果称该定制聚合物的刚性比业内其他材料最高高出40%；屏幕下方还设有钛金属板，定制胶层允许各层像书页一样滑动，以缓解弯折应力。苹果没有针对这段屏幕被按压后变软、起皱的现象作出回应。
爆料者Ice Universe推测，这种手感可能与可变厚度超薄玻璃有关：铰链位置采用较薄玻璃以便弯折，两侧则更厚以增强强度。康宁确实介绍过类似的VtG玻璃设计，但苹果并未确认iPhone Duo采用该材料，因此这种解释仍属猜测。
这也不代表屏幕表面已有永久折痕。用户视频显示，按压形成的纹路在松手后似乎会消失；但反复弯折和长期使用是否会造成损伤，目前尚无公开测试结果。iPhone Duo内屏保护层可更换，不过这并不能说明铰链区域的柔软现象只涉及保护层，具体原因仍有待苹果进一步说明。

units.text: 在获得创纪录的57亿美元专利侵权判决后，美国专利持有公司Taction正寻求进一步提高苹果的赔偿金额，希望法院将2026年部分产品销售纳入赔偿范围，并追加数亿美元规模的判决前利息。
此前，陪审团裁定苹果侵犯了Taction持有的两项专利，但认定相关侵权行为并非故意实施。苹果始终否认存在不当行为，并已对这一总额达57亿美元的判决提出上诉。
据报道，Taction近日向联邦法官提交申请，要求Apple Pay更多赔偿。该公司认为，目前确定的赔偿金额仅覆盖2021年至2026年3月之间的相关销售活动，而在此之后的约六个月时间内，苹果仍持续销售涉及案件的产品，因此赔偿范围应进一步扩大，将额外期间的销售收入纳入计算。
除追加损害赔偿外，Taction还要求按照加利福尼亚州法定7%的利率计算判决前利息。考虑到57亿美元的赔偿基数，仅利息部分就可能达到极为可观的金额，在原本已经巨大的赔偿额之外再增加数亿美元负担。
Taction向法院表示，陪审团作出的赔偿金额规模虽然庞大，但这并不应成为拒绝支付利息的理由。在其看来，相关利息属于正常法律救济的一部分，应当依法计算并支付。
与此同时，苹果仍在积极挑战这项裁决。公司认为，陪审团在确定损害赔偿金额时缺乏充分依据，相关计算方式存在问题，因此判决结果并不可靠。
苹果还主张，案件本身的法律逻辑以及所谓侵权认定之间存在矛盾，希望通过后续司法程序推翻整项裁决，甚至争取获得有利于自己的简易判决结果。不过，截至目前，法院尚未就苹果的相关请求作出最终决定。
此次争议源于涉及iPhone和Apple Watch触觉反馈技术的专利诉讼。若Taction的最新请求获得支持，苹果面临的潜在赔偿责任将进一步增加，使这场已创下美国专利诉讼赔偿纪录的案件继续升级。

units.text: High fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions in the EU are said to be holding up wider third-party adoption of the NFC chip in an iPhone, and the UK is instead looking for easier access, and no cost.

Following both the UK's 2024 investigation into digital wallets, and Apple's agreement to open NFC access in Europe, the country's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) wants more. It argues that if Apple offers the same terms for UK developers, it will still be insufficient.

Consequently it wants easier access with fewer conditions. The CMA argues that none of this raises any security concerns, and that its proposals are needed to help UK businesses benefit from the technology.

"We have heard that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions relating to Apple's contactless technology make it too difficult for challengers to innovate and compete," said Sarah Cardell, Chief Executive of the CMA, in a statement. "By removing barriers to entry, we can help create the conditions for brilliant British businesses with great ideas to develop new products and services here — from payment apps and digital IDs to travel passes and digital keys."
The CMA notes that no firms have released an alternative to Apple Wallet in the UK, while five have in Europe. The first of those was Vipps, which launched in Norway in 2024.

According to the CMA, it is Apple's fees and access rules that are preventing rivals developing digital wallets. However, Apple has told AppleInsider and other venues that it disagrees with the UK's CMA.

"We do not believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections," said Apple in a statement. "We will continue to engage constructively to reach an outcome that is in the best interest of our users."
The CMA is currently presenting its proposals as a consultation. It is inviting comments until November 17, 2026, and says it will issue its decision shortly afterwards.

units.text: Skyrim Comes to Apple Silicon Macs With New Unofficial Installer

Bethesda's beloved role-playing game "The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim" has reached multiple generations of consoles since its 2011 debut, but it never officially came to the Mac. A new unofficial project called SkyrimMT now aims to make playing and modding it on Apple silicon Macs easier than ever.

Mac owners have found ways to play Skyrim over the years, including installing Windows through Boot Camp on Intel Macs and using compatibility software such as CrossOver. Boot Camp is unavailable on Apple silicon Macs, leaving players dependent on other solutions to run the Windows game.

SkyrimMT's appeal is in bringing that process together in an app built specifically for Skyrim. Its automated setup installs the required compatibility software and guides users through signing in to Steam and installing their copy of the game. It supports Skyrim Special Edition and Anniversary Edition.

Its native mod manager supports browsing Nexus Mods, installing Nexus Collections and Wabbajack modlists, and importing Mod Organizer 2 setups. Common additions such as Skyrim Script Extender and SkyUI can also be installed through the app. Users can maintain separate mod profiles, inspect conflicts, sort load orders, and restore earlier configurations from snapshots.
Under the hood, SkyrimMT runs the Windows game through Wine and uses DXMT to translate its Direct3D 11 graphics to Apple's Metal.

SkyrimMT requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS Ventura 13 or later, approximately 25GB of free storage, and a Steam copy of the game. The open-source app is available from the project's GitHub releases page.

evidence.discovery_lead: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，一个开源的 macOS 原生静态重编译项目现已能够在 Apple Silicon 设备上运行《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》。在基础款 M4 MacBook Air 上，这款游戏可以稳定跑到 90 帧，性能表现优于任天堂 Switch 2 官方版本，同时也超过另一款非官方 PC 移植版本。 IT之家注意到，开发者 liyong 开源了 MacNativeGames 项目，这是一个非官方静态重编译工程，可以将《王国之泪》转换为 ARM64 架构的 macOS（以及 iOS）原生应用。该移植版本直接调用苹果 Metal 4 图形接口，最高支持 4K 分辨率的 MetalFX 超分技术，除原生键盘操控外，还支持索尼 DualSense 手柄与 Xbox 手柄。 实际上，该版本性能强于模组制作者 NotRexed 开发的非官方 x86 PC 静态重编译版本。后者在英伟达 RTX 4060 Ti 显卡上帧率仅在 32 至 59 帧之间波动。不过这款 x86 重编译项目仍在持续开发，后续还会推出更多更新。 相比传统模拟器，性能提升源于架构层面的兼容性。任天堂 Switch 的 Tegra X1 芯片与苹果 M 系列芯片都采用 ARM64 指令集。因此 Switch 程序里的 AArch64 机器码，可以在运行前直接转译为 macOS 原生 ARM64 可执行文件。 该方案还消除了一大图形性能瓶颈。过去在 macOS 上模拟 Switch 游戏，需要先将 Switch 专属 NVN 图形 API 转为 Vulkan，再通过 MoltenVK 把 Vulkan 封装适配到苹果 Metal 接口。静态重编译则完全省去这两层转译，直接对接 Metal 4。 海拉鲁地图体量庞大，在运行时编译着色器会导致玩家进入新区域时出现明显卡顿。为解决该问题，MacNativeGames 采用众包方式收集已解析的着色器与资源清单，编译器可以在游戏启动前预先完成着色器构建。 但在准备打开 MacBook 尝试之前需要注意，这并非一款可一键安装的应用。为避免分发任天堂受版权保护的代码，GitHub 仓库仅提供重编译工具。用户需要自行准备从已破解 Switch 设备上合法导出的.xci 或.nsp 游戏文件、 prod.keys 文件以及固件字体文件，再借助苹果 Xcode 命令行工具在本地编译生成.app 程序。 随着 AI 代码工具不断进步，整个静态重编译圈子正在发生变化。以往需要数年才能取得的成果，如今短短数周就能实现。

units.text: 苹果公司于10月20日宣布，正式开始为iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max以及搭载M5 Max、M5 Ultra芯片的Mac Studio和搭载M6或M5 Pro芯片的Mac mini提供官方维修零件销售服务，进一步扩大其自助维修计划（Self Service Repair）的覆盖范围。
苹果于2022年推出自助维修计划，允许符合条件地区的用户购买原厂更换零件，并购买或租赁维修所需工具，自行完成设备维修。同时，苹果还为多款产品提供官方维修手册，详细说明各类可更换零部件的维修流程和操作步骤。
此次更新后，苹果自助维修商店已新增对多款近期发布设备的支持。值得注意的是，这项扩展与苹果当天公布的新供应链合作消息同步进行。苹果表示，更多美国供应商正在参与iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone Duo相关零部件的生产制造。
对于iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max用户而言，现在可以购买多种官方替换零件及配套维修工具，涵盖后盖玻璃、电池、底部扬声器、摄像头模组、显示屏、机身外壳、前置摄像头、逻辑主板、主麦克风、SIM卡托、Taptic Engine触觉反馈组件、顶部扬声器以及其他零部件。
在选择相应维修类别后，用户不仅可以购买替换零件，还能获取对应维修所需的工具和耗材，包括粘合剂切割工具、吸盘、尼龙探针、胶水清除工具、扭矩螺丝刀以及各类螺丝等。这些工具和配件也可单独购买。
价格方面，iPhone 18 Pro系列的官方后置摄像头模组售价为249美元。尽管该机型新增了可变光圈系统，但摄像头替换价格与上一代机型保持一致。苹果同时提供旧件回收返还计划，用户归还原摄像头后可获得59.76美元返还，实际维修成本可降至189.24美元。
针对Mac Studio机型，苹果现已提供从Thunderbolt和USB-C接口到风扇、扬声器、SSD存储模块、逻辑主板以及电源模块等几乎全部主要部件的官方替换零件。
相较之下，Mac mini可购买的维修部件数量略少，但仍覆盖风扇、扬声器、逻辑主板、电池、电源模块等核心组件以及其他常见维修项目。
随着此次扩展，苹果自助维修计划已进一步向高端iPhone和最新Mac产品线开放，让具备技术能力的用户能够直接获取官方零件、工具和维修资料，在授权维修中心之外获得更多维修选择。

units.text: UK Proposes New Ways to Help Apple Pay Rivals
The UK's competition regulator has proposed changes to make it easier and cheaper for companies to offer alternatives to Apple Pay on the iPhone (via Reuters).

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) says Apple's fees and restrictions make it too difficult for rivals to launch contactless payment apps. Its proposals would give developers more ways to access the iPhone's NFC technology, which allows users to pay by holding their device near a payment terminal.

Apple opened up NFC access to developers in the UK in 2024, but companies must sign an agreement with Apple and pay fees. They also have to use the iPhone's Secure Element, which is a chip that stores sensitive information such as payment credentials.

The CMA wants Apple to also support host card emulation (HCE), an alternative that lets payment apps work without using the Secure Element. It also proposes rules that it expects would substantially lower Apple's access fees, although it would still allow the company to charge something.

Apple already offers HCE access for free in the European Union under commitments agreed in 2024. The CMA highlights that rival payment apps have since launched in the EU, while no competing wallet-type product has launched in the UK under Apple's current terms.
Apple told Reuters that developers can already offer contactless services using its technology:

We do not believe the CMA should require ​Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections. We will continue to engage constructively to reach ​an outcome that is in the best interest of our users.

The CMA said the evidence it reviewed did not suggest either approach was inherently insecure. The proposals are open for consultation until November 17, 2026. The CMA will make a final decision after reviewing responses.

units.text: 英国竞争与市场管理局（CMA）提出新方案，计划让英国企业更容易开发可替代Apple Pay的iPhone钱包和非接触式服务。CMA认为，苹果目前的接入费用、合同条款和技术限制，让部分金融科技公司难以建立可行的商业模式；这仍是公开征询意见的提案，并非已生效的新规。
苹果在2024年已向英国开发者开放iPhone的近场通信（NFC）功能，但企业必须与苹果签约、支付费用，并使用设备中的安全元件（Secure Element）保存支付凭证。CMA拟要求苹果同时支持国际上常用的两种接入方式：安全元件方案，以及主机卡模拟（HCE）。前者把敏感信息保存在设备内的安全芯片中，后者则通过设备外部的方式处理相关信息，让开发者有更多技术选择。
CMA没有打算直接规定接入价格，而是拟定收费原则，目标是让费用明显低于苹果目前收取的水平，同时仍允许苹果因提供技术接入而收费。英国监管机构表示，审查到的证据没有显示安全元件或HCE本身存在固有安全问题。苹果则称，开发者已经能够使用其技术提供非接触服务，并反对强制采用其认为隐私和安全保护较弱的方案。
CMA称，欧盟在2024年要求苹果开放相关技术后，Vipps在六个月内推出首个替代支付应用，随后PayPal、Klarna、Curve和BBVA也上线相关服务；英国目前尚无钱包类产品在苹果现行条款下推出。若方案落地，潜在应用不只限于支付，还包括数字身份和年龄验证、交通票证、汽车或酒店电子钥匙，以及会员积分服务。
CMA数据显示，非接触支付已占英国全部支付交易的39%，超过六成成年人使用数字钱包，Apple Wallet是当地最受欢迎的选择。此次提案依据英国《2024年数字市场、竞争与消费者法》提出，公众咨询将于2026年11月17日结束；CMA将在评估意见后作出最终决定。

units.text: Apple acquires a variety of companies every year, and recently many of its acquisitions—including the latest, Samplab—have revolved around one clear goal: improving and expanding Apple Creator Studio.
Apple has prioritized Creator Studio with recent acquisitions, strengthening ecosystem for creatives
Next week, Apple is expected to unveil four new hardware products aimed at creatives: a redesigned MacBook Pro with touch, modernized iPad mini, and M6 versions of the iMac and MacBook Pro.
But hardware is only one part of Apple’s creator-focused push.
All year long, the company has sought to strengthen its ecosystem of tools for creatives by launching Apple Creator Studio and acquiring companies that expand its feature set.
Apple Creator Studio debuted in January as a suite of pro apps for creatives, such as Pixelmator Pro, Logic Pro, Final Cut Pro, and more.
The service has regularly rolled out new features since launch, but we’ve also seen Apple invest behind-the-scenes with acquisitions that clearly have Creator Studio in mind.

In the spring we learned of two acquisitions that fit the bill. MotionVFX provided “visual effects templates, plugins, and motion graphics tools” for Final Cut Pro. Color.io brought tools for “color management and grading of digital imaging,” likely with Final Cut and/or Pixelmator in mind.

Now the latest acquisition revealed yesterday, Samplab, pitched itself as the “ultimate audio editor for musicians,” making its features a natural fit for Logic Pro. And even the recent acqui-hire of Huxe could have Creator Studio benefits too.

Why invest so much in Creator Studio? Obviously the chance to grow services revenue is reason enough. But I suspect the company also sees the app suite as a key component of its overall pitch to creatives.

Apple has long focused on bringing hardware, software, and services together in a seamless ecosystem. And its recent efforts on the software and services side are set to dovetail nicely with next week’s new hardware. All this to say, expect to see Creator Studio apps get some spotlight during Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ announcements on October 28.
Do you subscribe to Apple Creator Studio? If not, what’s it missing for you? Let us know in the comments.
